value.title: GraphBackend interface + extract TokensaveBackend (tokensave byte-identical)
value.description: Introduce a GraphBackend abstraction that owns the per-engine tool catalog, param builders, and response-shape adapters, and refactor GraphClient to delegate to an injected backend. Move the tokensave-specific pieces out of src/graph/client.ts — TOOL (client.ts:31-37), QUERY_TOOL (40-45), the Ts*Row raw types (52-109), and toNodeRef (116-131) — into a new src/graph/backends/tokensave-backend.ts implementing the interface. GraphClient keeps ALL of its cross-cutting logic (runWithSandbox/runRaw, sandbox keepNode, staleness cache, health short-circuit, GRAPH_DISABLED/UNAVAILABLE, GraphFallback, prefetch dispatch) and instead of a hardcoded TOOL name + inline narrow, asks the backend for {tool, params, narrow} per operation. Construction sites keep passing a concrete TokensaveBackend so behavior is byte-identical. No config, detection, or code-review-graph work in this sprint.

successCriteria.description: Build + typecheck pass with zero errors (npm run build, npm run typecheck).

A GraphBackend interface (new src/graph/backends/types.ts or similar) declares, for each logical operation used by GraphClient (search, query[callers_of|callees_of|imports_of|tests_for], impact, reviewContext, overview, changes), a way to obtain the MCP tool name, build the params object, and narrow the raw MCP payload into the shared type (SearchHit[] | NodeRef[] | ImpactReport | string). It also carries an engine `id` (e.g. 'tokensave').

src/graph/backends/tokensave-backend.ts implements GraphBackend and contains the tokensave_* tool names + Ts*Row narrowing that previously lived in client.ts, producing identical outputs (same NodeRef/SearchHit/ImpactReport values for the same raw input).

GraphClient no longer references any tokensave_* string or Ts*Row type; it delegates tool-name/params/narrow to the injected backend. Its public method signatures (search/query/impact/reviewContext/overview/changes/prefetch) and GraphResult return shapes are unchanged. A grep for `tokensave_` over src/graph/client.ts returns zero matches; over src/graph/backends/tokensave-backend.ts it returns the catalog.

Cross-cutting behavior is preserved: sandbox post-filter (keepNode), staleness cache (checkStaleness), GRAPH_DISABLED short-circuit when config.enabled=false, GRAPH_UNAVAILABLE on broken/restarting health, toFailureResult mapping, and prefetch dispatch all behave exactly as before. Existing tests/graph/client.test.ts passes unchanged (adjusting only the construction to inject a TokensaveBackend).
The full existing test suite is green with no NEW failures (pre-existing unrelated failures such as cockpit-integration MCP E2E may remain). With backend=tokensave the graph path is byte-identical.
lint passes (zero errors); ESM .js import specifiers, `import type`, unicode section-header comments, no synchronous fs are preserved.

nonGoals: Do NOT add config.graph.backend, auto-detection, or resolveGraphBackend — that is Sprint 3.
Do NOT touch the MCP transport serveArgs, prereq, or CLI wrapper yet — that is Sprint 2.
Do NOT add any code-review-graph code, tool names, or fixtures.
Do NOT change GraphClient public method signatures, the GraphResult union, or NodeRef/SearchHit/ImpactReport in src/graph/types.ts.
Do NOT change GraphFallback, the circuit breaker, PID/orphan handling, or the sandbox algorithm.
stopConditions: GraphClient delegates every tool-name/params/narrow to an injected GraphBackend; TokensaveBackend reproduces the old behavior; build/typecheck/test/lint green; tokensave path byte-identical
value.definitionOfDone: A GraphBackend interface exists; TokensaveBackend implements it holding the tokensave_* catalog + Ts*Row narrows extracted from client.ts; GraphClient delegates to the injected backend while keeping all sandbox/staleness/health/fallback/prefetch logic and its public signatures; existing tests pass unchanged (with a TokensaveBackend injected at construction); build/typecheck/test green, lint clean.
assumptions: client.ts today hardcodes TOOL (31-37) and QUERY_TOOL (40-45) and does per-method narrowing inline (search 168-186, query 188-245, impact 247-268, reviewContext 270-273, overview 275-281, changes 283-294). runWithSandbox (366-401) already isolates the call+narrow+sandbox pattern; the cleanest refactor is to have each public method ask the backend for a {tool, params, narrow} triple and pass narrow into runWithSandbox unchanged.
toNodeRef (116-131) + NODE_KINDS (114) coercion move into the tokensave backend (they are tokensave-row-shaped). The shared types NodeRef/SearchHit/ImpactReport stay in types.ts.

GraphClient's constructor currently takes (projectRoot, mcpClient, artifactStore, fallback, incidents, config). Add the backend as an injected dependency (constructor param or setter). Update the two construction sites that build GraphClient directly — pipeline-lifecycle.ts getGraphClient (222-249) and cli/commands/onboard.ts (107-114) — to pass a `new TokensaveBackend()`.
The mcpClient.call<unknown>(tool, params) contract (client.ts:387) is unchanged; only WHERE the tool string + params + narrow come from changes.

tests/graph/client.test.ts makeClient (line 70) constructs a GraphClient; it will need to inject a TokensaveBackend. The raw MCP responses the test feeds stay identical, so assertions on the narrowed output stay identical.
value.generatorNotes:
Read FIRST in full: src/graph/client.ts (all of it — the TOOL/QUERY_TOOL maps, the Ts*Row types, every public method, runWithSandbox/runRaw, keepNode), src/graph/types.ts (shared types), tests/graph/client.test.ts (makeClient + the per-method assertions). This is a pure refactor: same inputs -> same outputs.

DESIGN the GraphBackend interface to expose, per operation, either (a) a method returning {tool: string, params: unknown, narrow: (raw:unknown)=>T}, or (b) direct methods the client calls. Recommended shape: an object with `id: string` and one method per op, e.g. `searchPlan(q, opts) -> {tool, params, narrow}`, `queryPlan(pattern, target) -> {tool, params, narrow}`, `impactPlan(target)`, `reviewContextPlan(nodes)`, `overviewPlan()`, `changesPlan(since)`. GraphClient's method bodies then become: `const {tool, params, narrow} = this.backend.searchPlan(q, opts); return this.runWithSandbox(tool, params, (raw)=>narrow(raw).filter(h=>this.keepNode(h.node,'search')))`. Keep the sandbox filtering IN GraphClient (it needs projectRoot + incidents); the backend only produces the raw-typed value.

MOVE to src/graph/backends/tokensave-backend.ts: TOOL, QUERY_TOOL, all Ts*Row types, toNodeRef, NODE_KINDS. Implement each *Plan method to return the same tool + params + narrow logic that client.ts currently inlines (e.g. searchPlan.narrow maps TsSearchRow[] -> SearchHit[] via toNodeRef, applies the opts.kind post-filter). Put the interface in src/graph/backends/types.ts (or fold into src/graph/types.ts if cleaner) and export GraphBackend.

WIRE construction: pipeline-lifecycle.ts getGraphClient and cli/commands/onboard.ts pass `new TokensaveBackend()`. Update tests/graph/client.test.ts makeClient to inject it.

VERIFY: `npm run build && npm run typecheck && npx vitest run tests/graph/` then the full suite. grep -n 'tokensave_' src/graph/client.ts must be empty. Commit `bober(sprint-1): GraphBackend interface + extract TokensaveBackend, GraphClient delegates`.
value.evaluatorNotes: This sprint's whole point is BYTE-IDENTICAL tokensave behavior via a new seam. sc-1-4: `grep -n 'tokensave_' src/graph/client.ts` MUST be empty and the same grep over src/graph/backends/tokensave-backend.ts must show the catalog — confirm the extraction actually happened (not just an alias re-export from client.ts). sc-1-3/1-5: read tokensave-backend.ts and confirm the narrow logic matches the old client.ts (same toNodeRef coercion, same opts.kind post-filter in search, same callers/callees/imports/tests mapping, same impact root/affected/testsAffected partition, same changes mapping). sc-1-5: confirm keepNode/sandbox, staleness, GRAPH_DISABLED, GRAPH_UNAVAILABLE, prefetch dispatch still live in GraphClient and are unchanged. sc-1-6: run the full suite; assert NO new failures vs baseline (git stash to compare if unsure). Reject if any tokensave_* string or Ts*Row type remains in client.ts, or if any public GraphClient signature changed.

value.title: Fold process spec + prereq + CLI map into the backend; parameterize the transport (tokensave byte-identical)
value.description: Extend the GraphBackend abstraction (Sprint 1) with the remaining engine-specific surface so a backend fully describes how to run its engine: a ProcessSpec (binary name + serve args), a PrereqSpec (version command, compatible-version predicate, install hint), and a CliMap (init/sync/status commands + output parsers). Parameterize the MCP transport so it spawns `binary + serveArgs` from the backend's ProcessSpec instead of the hardcoded execa(this.binary, ['serve']) at mcp-client.ts:242. Make TokensavePrereqCheck (src/graph/prereq.ts) and TokensaveCli (src/graph/cli.ts) either driven by, or produced from, the tokensave backend's specs. Still tokensave-only; construction sites keep building a TokensaveBackend. Behavior byte-identical.

successCriteria.description: Build + typecheck pass with zero errors.

GraphBackend gains a ProcessSpec {binary, serveArgs} accessor. The MCP transport spawns `execa(spec.binary, spec.serveArgs)` derived from the backend; for tokensave this resolves to binary 'tokensave' (or cfg.tokensavePath) and serveArgs ['serve'] — identical to today. A unit test asserts the spawn argv for the tokensave backend is ['serve'].

GraphBackend gains a PrereqSpec: version command args (['--version']), a compatible-version predicate (tokensave: semver satisfies '>=6.0.0-beta.1 <7.0.0'), and an install hint (tokensave: the existing brew/scoop/cargo per-platform strings, VERBATIM). The prereq check derives these from the backend; the tokensave hints and range are unchanged. A unit test (execa mocked) asserts tokensave version 6.1.1 passes and an out-of-range version fails with the existing incompatible hint.

GraphBackend gains a CliMap describing init/sync/status commands + output parsers. For tokensave: init->['init'], sync->['sync', ...paths], status->['status','--json'], with the existing parseSyncOutput/status parsing. The short-lived CLI wrapper runs the backend's commands. A unit test asserts tokensave sync output '3 added, 1 modified, 0 removed' parses to indexed=4 (unchanged behavior).

The transport class no longer contains the engine-specific literal 'tokensave' default binary or ['serve'] literal in a way that other engines can't override; engine specifics come from the injected backend. (The class may keep a generic name; tokensave strings live only in the tokensave backend module.)

The full existing test suite is green with no NEW failures; with backend=tokensave the prereq, transport spawn, init/sync/status, and query paths are byte-identical. Real-binary skipIf integration tests still pass against tokensave 6.1.1 when present (start handshake + a tokensave_status round-trip).
lint passes; diff confined to the graph layer (backends/*, mcp-client.ts, prereq.ts, cli.ts + their tests) plus the construction sites that already inject the backend.

nonGoals: Do NOT add config.graph.backend or auto-detection yet — that is Sprint 3 (this sprint only makes the backend able to DESCRIBE its process/prereq/cli).
Do NOT add code-review-graph specs.
Do NOT change the circuit-breaker math, health-state machine, PID/orphan handling, or the MCP initialize/tools-call wire protocol.
Do NOT change public GraphClient signatures or shared types.
stopConditions: A tokensave backend fully describes its process/prereq/cli specs, the transport spawns from ProcessSpec, and tokensave behavior is byte-identical with build/typecheck/test/lint green
value.definitionOfDone: GraphBackend carries ProcessSpec + PrereqSpec + CliMap; the transport spawns binary+serveArgs from the backend; prereq and init/sync/status run the backend's specs; tokensave strings (binary, serve, version range, install hints, cli verbs) live only in the tokensave backend module; existing tests + skipIf integration tests pass unchanged.
assumptions: Transport spawn: mcp-client.ts spawnAndHandshake (line 242) does `execa(this.binary, ['serve'], ...)`. Replace ['serve'] with serveArgs sourced from the backend's ProcessSpec; keep the binary resolution (cfg.tokensavePath ?? spec.binary). Everything else in the transport (handshake, tools/call envelope, breaker, health) stays identical.

Prereq: prereq.ts TokensavePrereqCheck runs `<binary> --version` (13), matches a semver (25), checks TOKENSAVE_VERSION_RANGE (5,34-38), and returns per-platform install hints (48-58). Refactor so a generic prereq check takes the backend's PrereqSpec {versionArgs, isCompatible(version), installHint()}; keep TOKENSAVE_VERSION_RANGE + the exact hint strings inside the tokensave backend (they are marked 'verbatim, DO NOT paraphrase').

CLI: cli.ts TokensaveCli runs init/sync/status with tokensave-specific args and parseSyncOutput (187-220) + status JSON parsing (128-174). Refactor so a generic short-lived CLI takes the backend's CliMap {initArgs, syncArgs(paths), statusArgs, parseSync(output), parseStatus(stdout)}; keep tokensave parsing inside the tokensave backend.

Construction sites (pipeline-lifecycle.ts:77-79,95-100,105-109; onboard.ts:70,87-92; plus mcp/server.ts, cli/impact.ts, cli/graph.ts) currently pass cfg.tokensavePath ?? 'tokensave' into these classes. After this sprint they pass the tokensave backend (or its specs). Auto-selection of WHICH backend is Sprint 3 — here they still hardcode the tokensave backend.
The class name TokensaveMcpClient may be kept for now (a rename to a generic name is optional and can be a follow-up); what matters is it takes serveArgs from the backend, not a hardcoded ['serve'].

value.title: Backend selection: graph.backend config + auto-detection + wire construction sites + additive manifest
value.description: Add an optional graph.backend config field and a resolveGraphBackend() that decides which engine to run: an explicit graph.backend value wins; otherwise auto-detect by probing each engine's version command (tokensave preferred when both succeed); when neither is installed, surface a combined install hint naming both. Wire all five construction sites (pipeline-lifecycle.ts, mcp/server.ts, cli/impact.ts, cli/graph.ts, cli/onboard.ts) to resolve the backend instead of hardcoding the tokensave backend. Evolve GraphManifest additively to record `backend` + `backendVersion` (keep tokensaveVersion; old manifests default backend='tokensave'). A CodeReviewGraphBackend stub is registered so detection can select it, but its adapters/fixtures come in Sprints 4-6.

successCriteria.description: Build + typecheck pass with zero errors.

GraphSectionSchema gains an optional `backend` enum ('tokensave' | 'code-review-graph'), default undefined (=auto-detect). A config with no backend field loads and validates exactly as before (schema back-compat).

resolveGraphBackend(config, {probe}) returns the tokensave backend when graph.backend='tokensave' or when unset and only tokensave is detected; returns the code-review-graph backend when graph.backend='code-review-graph' or when unset and only code-review-graph is detected; prefers tokensave when unset and BOTH are detected. Unit-tested with the version probe mocked (no real binaries).

When graph.backend is unset and NEITHER binary is detected, resolution fails with a combined install hint that names BOTH engines (tokensave install hint AND `pip install code-review-graph`). Unit-tested with both probes failing.

An explicit graph.backend value short-circuits detection (no probe of the other engine) and is honored even if that engine's binary is missing (the prereq check then fails with that engine's install hint, not a combined one). Unit-tested.

All five construction sites resolve the backend via resolveGraphBackend and pass it into the transport/prereq/cli/GraphClient: src/graph/pipeline-lifecycle.ts, src/mcp/server.ts, src/cli/commands/impact.ts, src/cli/commands/graph.ts, src/cli/commands/onboard.ts. With graph.backend unset + tokensave installed, every one behaves byte-identically to today.

GraphManifest adds `backend: string` and `backendVersion: string` additively; GraphArtifactStore reads legacy manifests (missing backend -> 'tokensave', backendVersion falls back to tokensaveVersion) without error. Unit-tested with an old-shape manifest fixture.
Full suite green (no NEW failures); lint clean. With graph.backend unset and tokensave present, `agent-bober onboard`/`impact`/`graph` and the run pipeline are byte-identical to before this spec.

nonGoals: Do NOT implement code-review-graph response adapters, tool catalog, or fixtures — a stub backend (id + process/prereq/cli specs only, adapters throwing GRAPH_UNAVAILABLE / marked TODO) is enough for detection to select it. Adapters land in Sprints 4-6.
Do NOT change the tokensave path behavior when backend is unset or 'tokensave'.
Do NOT add per-command --backend CLI flags (config field + auto-detect only, per the selection decision).
Do NOT remove tokensaveVersion from the manifest (kept for back-compat).
stopConditions: graph.backend config + resolveGraphBackend auto-detection wire all five construction sites; combined-hint-when-neither; tokensave path byte-identical when unset; manifest evolves additively; build/typecheck/test/lint green
value.definitionOfDone: An optional graph.backend enum + resolveGraphBackend (explicit-wins, else auto-detect with tokensave preference, combined install hint when neither) drives all five construction sites; the CodeReviewGraphBackend stub is registered for detection; the manifest carries additive backend/backendVersion with legacy read; the tokensave path is byte-identical when backend is unset; suite + lint green.
assumptions: Schema: src/config/schema.ts GraphSectionSchema (394-417). Add `backend: z.enum(['tokensave','code-review-graph']).optional()`. Also consider an optional `codeReviewGraphPath: z.string().optional()` mirroring tokensavePath for a custom cr-graph binary path (additive).

Detection probe = run `<binary> --version` (reuse the prereq versionArgs) and treat exit 0 + a parseable version as 'installed'. resolveGraphBackend takes an injectable probe(binary, args)->{ok, version} so tests mock it. Registry: a list of known backends [tokensaveBackend, codeReviewGraphBackend], each exposing id + processSpec.binary + prereqSpec.

Preference order when unset + both installed: tokensave first (explicit product decision). When exactly one installed: that one. When none: throw/return a structured failure whose hint concatenates both backends' installHint() for the current platform.

Construction sites all currently read cfg.tokensavePath ?? 'tokensave' (pipeline-lifecycle.ts:77,95-100,105-109; onboard.ts:70,87-92; and the impact/graph/mcp-server sites). Replace each with `const backend = await resolveGraphBackend(config, ...)` then pass backend down. The binary override becomes backend-specific (tokensavePath for tokensave, codeReviewGraphPath for cr-graph).

Manifest: src/graph/types.ts GraphManifest (13-22) + GraphArtifactStore read/write. Add backend + backendVersion; when reading a manifest lacking backend, default backend='tokensave' and backendVersion = existing tokensaveVersion. Keep tokensaveVersion written for tokensave for now.

The pipeline-lifecycle stub GraphSection object (pipeline-lifecycle.ts:230-248) already hardcodes a config; ensure it doesn't override the resolved backend — the backend is a separate injected dependency from the GraphSection config.

value.title: code-review-graph backend: process/prereq/CLI specs + capture live fixtures
value.description: Flesh out CodeReviewGraphBackend's non-adapter surface and capture ground-truth fixtures. Implement its ProcessSpec (binary 'code-review-graph', serveArgs ['serve']), PrereqSpec (versionArgs ['--version'], a compatible-version predicate, installHint 'pip install code-review-graph'), and CliMap (init->build, sync->update, status->detect-changes/status with output parsers). Then PROBE the locally-installed `code-review-graph serve` to capture the REAL MCP tool output JSON for every tool the adapters will need, and commit those as fixtures under tests/graph/fixtures/cr-graph/. Use `git show 6ed3f77~1:src/graph/client.ts` (agent-bober's original code-review-graph adapter) as a shape reference. No response adapters yet — those consume these fixtures in Sprints 5-6.

successCriteria.description: Build + typecheck pass with zero errors.

CodeReviewGraphBackend.processSpec = {binary:'code-review-graph' (overridable via config.graph.codeReviewGraphPath), serveArgs:['serve']}; prereqSpec.installHint = 'pip install code-review-graph'; the generalized prereq detects a real `code-review-graph --version` (skipIf-gated integration test) and, with execa mocked, a valid version passes and a clearly-incompatible one fails with the pip install hint.

CliMap maps init->['build'], sync->['update', ...paths] (or the documented incremental verb), status->the detect-changes/status verb, each with an output parser. parseSync/parseStatus are unit-tested against captured CLI output samples.

Real MCP tool output JSON is captured from a live `code-review-graph serve` (via the initialize + tools/call probe) for every tool the adapters need — at minimum semantic_search_nodes_tool, get_impact_radius_tool, get_review_context_tool, get_architecture_overview_tool, detect_changes_tool, query_graph_tool, traverse_graph_tool — and committed as tests/graph/fixtures/cr-graph/<tool>.json. Each fixture is the exact unwrapped payload (result.content[].text parsed) the transport would hand an adapter.

resolveGraphBackend selects the code-review-graph backend when config.graph.backend='code-review-graph' and, in an integration context, when only cr-graph is installed. A skipIf-gated integration test starts a real `code-review-graph serve` and completes the MCP initialize handshake through the (Sprint-2 parameterized) transport.

If the live cr-graph binary cannot be located during this sprint, the sprint DOES NOT invent shapes: it records the blocker in the sprint notes, seeds fixtures from the git-history reference (6ed3f77~1) marked as provisional, and leaves a documented follow-up to refresh them from a live run. (This criterion is satisfied by either a real capture OR an explicit, documented provisional-fixture fallback — never by silently guessed JSON.)
Full suite green (no NEW failures); tokensave path unaffected; lint clean.

nonGoals: Do NOT implement the response adapters (search/impact/etc. narrowing) — Sprints 5-6 consume these fixtures.
Do NOT add a live cr-graph test to the DEFAULT CI path — cr-graph integration tests must be skipIf-gated on the binary being present.
Do NOT modify the tokensave backend or the shared transport wire protocol.
Do NOT install code-review-graph for the user or add it as an npm/pip dependency of this project.
stopConditions: CodeReviewGraphBackend has real process/prereq/cli specs, real (or explicitly-provisional) fixtures are committed for every needed tool, detection selects it, and the transport can initialize-handshake a real cr-graph serve; suite + lint green
value.definitionOfDone: CodeReviewGraphBackend describes its process/prereq/cli; committed fixtures under tests/graph/fixtures/cr-graph/ capture the real MCP output for every adapter tool (or documented-provisional from git history if the binary was unreachable, with a follow-up); detection + a skipIf live handshake work; tokensave path untouched; suite + lint green.
assumptions: code-review-graph is a Python 3.10+ package exposing `code-review-graph serve` (MCP) and CLI verbs build/update/watch/serve/detect-changes/daemon (per its README). Its ~30 MCP tools include semantic_search_nodes_tool, get_impact_radius_tool, get_review_context_tool, query_graph_tool, detect_changes_tool, traverse_graph_tool, get_architecture_overview_tool, build_or_update_graph_tool. Store dir is .code-review-graph/.

The binary was NOT on this shell's PATH at plan time (likely a venv/pipx install). The generator must LOCATE it: try `command -v code-review-graph`, `python -m code_review_graph --version`, common venv paths, or ask via config.graph.codeReviewGraphPath. If truly unreachable, invoke the sc-4-6 provisional-fixture fallback.
